items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: The last one that was here was my drummer, Fats Martin... he took the remnants of my band and kept going when I gave up.

ctx.x: No. The last one that was here was my drummer, Fats Martin, and he passed away, oh, about three or four years ago. Well, in fact, he took the remnants of my band and kept going when I gave up. And I stayed with him until he passed, and everybody knew him as a great drummer.
Is there anything else about the recording date, wherever those records made, for Vocalion? Here in town? Here in San Antonio.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-12-30
items.q: So I got Fats Martin which was a blessing in disguise. Because this guy turned out to be to me one of the greatest drummers that I'd ever heard.

ctx.x: You see Bernard Goldberg, a Jewish friend of mine that liked me from the first day that he met me. In fact this guy was driving a big black Pierce Hour in those days and he would go into me just like it was my car. So when I quit Charles Band in Dallas and I went back to New Orleans, he came down there and he told me, he said, why don't you get your band? Oh I said Mr. Goldberg, I'm a little too young for that. He said, go ahead and get your band, I'll get a job for you. In fact Bernard Goldberg had already had…

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: I stayed with him until he died. Got him baptized in the Catholic Church. I was his Godfather. And stayed and I went and carried his body.

ctx.x: Yeah, but you said Freddie and he played a dunk.
Well, I think that if you ever heard Fats Martin and you would listen to Freddie, you'll find out it's the same identical beats and everything else.
Yeah, well of course I wanted Freddie to tell me about it. Freddie said, oh, see, Don. That's the man you tell me about it.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: I've got to give credit to Fats Martin... Fats Martin was the greatest drumming that I've ever heard.

ctx.x: You had to change the style of the band, yeah. Yeah.

But there was always that, they said, there's something about this band that makes you want to dance. Well, I've got to give credit to Fats Martin. Now, if you close the curtain in front of Freddie Coleman, and close your eyes, you'd hear Fats Martin. It's almost identical. Fats Martin was the greatest drumming that I've ever heard. And he set the tempos. And it was something, now and then a fast number, which people would try to dance on, but they couldn't. It was mostly a feature number that featured musicians.

What about, I can't remember if I've answered this before. People in New Orleans have another language, I mean, not just the Creoles, but the whole, they picked up a lot of French and Spanish things here. What about in Texas? Do they say any of the same words over there? What do they say?
